resources.string: Flood survival, ready before the water arrives.
Version %1$s · offline flood survival app for Android

FloodCue keeps the information, warnings and messages you may need during a flood on your phone. It works without internet as much as possible, so you can prepare early, act quickly and ask for help even when the network is down.

• SOS Emergency Message — compose an emergency message with your GPS coordinates and a maps link, choose the contacts who receive it, and send it through your SMS app. A message queued while offline is sent automatically as soon as a network is back.

• One-tap SOS — the red SOS button on the home screen starts the siren and sends your help message with your location to your personal emergency contacts and the contacts you chose on the SOS screen, together, without any further taps.

• Emergency siren — plays a loud siren to attract nearby help; tap the button again to stop it.

• Flood checklist — a before-a-flood checklist in two layers, Essential and Complete, with progress tracking, covering go-bag supplies, phone readiness, home protection, family planning and evacuation.

• Safety tips — short, scannable tips for before, during and after a flood, with life-threatening warnings highlighted.

• Emergency guide — 16 situation-based guides ordered by urgency, such as trapped inside a rising home, trapped in a vehicle, no phone network, dying phone battery, snakes in floodwater, contaminated water and attracting rescuers.

• Offline maps — download your district's map once and open it without internet.

• Weather — temperature, current and next-24-hour rain probability and rainfall, and wind, read from Open-Meteo and cached for offline viewing.

• Flood alerts — official warnings from the NDMA SACHET feed, plus IMD district rainfall warnings when your own server key is configured, checked periodically in the background and announced with a loud alert notification.

• Offline communication — guidance and a shortcut to Bridgefy for mesh messaging when mobile networks are down.

• Emergency profile — your medical details, allergies and emergency contacts, saved so they are at hand when you need them.

FloodCue runs with two independent languages: the app language for menus, buttons, settings and screens, and the survival language for the checklist, safety tips and emergency guide. Change either one in Settings → Change language. English, Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam are offered; a language whose translation has not been added yet shows English text instead of breaking the screen.

Your phone numbers, medical details, checklist ticks and coordinates are stored on this phone. When you sign in, your profile — including emergency contacts and medical details — is stored on your own FloodCue account server so it follows your account, and it is never shared with anyone else, sold or used for advertising. Your location is read only when you ask for it, coordinates are never written to logs, and nothing is uploaded to any other service.\n\nFloodCue requests only the permissions its features need: location to add your coordinates, phone and SMS to call or send your emergency message, notifications for flood alerts, and internet for weather, alerts and your profile. Nothing is sent automatically in the background except the periodic flood-alert check.

• Official flood and heavy-rain warnings: NDMA SACHET public CAP feed (sachet.ndma.gov.in).
• District rainfall warnings: India Meteorological Department (IMD), read through your own proxy server because the IMD key is bound to one address.
• River and flood forecasts: Central Water Commission, opened as an official link because no reliable public machine-readable feed exists.
• Weather: Open-Meteo (open-meteo.com), a free open forecast API.

Warnings are reproduced as published. Rainfall forecasts alone never confirm that flooding is happening: always follow instructions from local authorities and disaster-management teams first.

• Opening your SMS app does not mean the message was delivered. Normal SMS needs cellular service; mobile data is not required. Sending SMS may be charged by your operator, so FloodCue always lets you review the recipients and confirm first.
• GPS needs a clear view of the sky. Indoors or under heavy cloud the coordinates may be missing or old — FloodCue labels an old position as the last known location instead of guessing a new one.
• Offline maps work only for the areas you downloaded.
• Background flood-alert checks run roughly every 15 minutes while the phone has connectivity, not continuously.
• FloodCue cannot call rescuers for you and does not replace official emergency services, evacuation orders or local warning signals.
Prepare before the water arrives, and follow official evacuation instructions above everything in this app.
